# AI Image Generation for Award-Winning Web Design — 2026 Research Dossier

**Scope:** hero backgrounds, full-bleed sections, textures, and art-directed imagery generated by hand in a browser (primarily Google Gemini) and dropped into a coded site. First real target: a **radiophysics / electronics / SDR / antennas university faculty** site.

**Method note:** WebSearch was unavailable for this research pass (session-wide budget exhausted before this task began). All verification below comes from 47 direct `WebFetch` calls against official vendor docs, Wikipedia, MDN, and museum/archive sites. Several vendor domains block automated fetches with Cloudflare 403s (docs.midjourney.com, ideogram.ai app pages, NASA's images.nasa.gov gallery, Smithsonian, Library of Congress, ESA, CERN copyright page, Adobe helpx, magnific pricing) — where that happened, the claim below is flagged **[established knowledge, not freshly re-verified]** rather than silently asserted. Everything else has a live citation. Full source list at the bottom.

**Quick picks for this project:** Gemini stays the daily driver (free, conversational, already the workflow). For anything with **lettering baked into the image**, switch to Ideogram. For a **vector faculty crest / iconography / diagram set**, use Recraft (true hex + SVG). If a Gemini hero is soft or under-detailed at hero scale, run it through **Krea's free enhancer** before shipping. Midjourney is worth the $10/mo only if the site needs genuinely painterly, art-directed atmosphere across many images fast — its style-reference consistency is unmatched. Skip Magnific/Firefly/Flux unless a specific gap shows up (respectively: extreme upscale, enterprise IP indemnity, self-hosted/open-weight pipeline).

## 2. Prompt craft that actually works

### 2.1 The universal anatomy (works as a mental checklist for any tool)

A prompt that reads like an art director wrote it, not a user, fills every one of these slots — in roughly this order:

1. **Shot type** — "wide establishing shot", "extreme macro", "elevated 3/4 view", "flat lay".
2. **Subject with 2–3 recognisable specifics** — not "an antenna" but "a Yagi-Uda antenna with seven aluminium elements and a corroded boom clamp". Specificity is what separates an art-directed image from generic stock.
3. **Technique / medium / process** — the vocabulary of an actual photographic or print process (see catalogue in §3). This one slot does more work than any other for "expensive-looking."
4. **Lighting setup** — source, direction, quality, colour temperature: "single hard sidelight from the left, deep shadow falloff, cool 5600K".
5. **Camera / lens / film or render engine** — "shot on a vintage 50mm at f/1.8, shallow depth of field" or "rendered in Octane, physically-based materials, ray-traced caustics".
6. **Colour palette** — named roles + hex where the tool supports it: "palette restricted to deep radar blue #0C3350, phosphor green #4DFFB4, void black #0A0E12".
7. **Composition + negative space** — explicit placement and an explicitly empty zone (see §4).
8. **Mood / era** — 2–3 adjectives, not a paragraph: "clinical, nocturnal, precise".
9. **Grain / texture / imperfection** — "fine 35mm film grain, slight halation on highlights" — this is what defeats the "smooth AI plastic" look.
10. **Negative constraints** — "no text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, no logo, no border or frame".
11. **Aspect ratio / parameters** — tool-specific syntax, always last.

### 2.2 Tool-specific syntax

**Midjourney** — parameters are appended to the end of the prompt, space-separated:
```
[prompt text] --ar 21:9 --style raw --stylize 250 --chaos 15 --sref https://example.com/ref.jpg --sw 400 --seed 918273 --no text, watermark, frame
```
- `--style raw` strips Midjourney's default "house beautification" for a more literal, less varnished read — usually the right call for a technical/editorial site.
- `--chaos 0–100` — variance between the four grid outputs; keep low (0–15) when you need a *set* of images to feel related.
- `--weird 0–3000` — pushes toward unusual compositions/materials; good for the more alien catalogue entries (ferrofluid, plasma, Kirlian), bad when you need predictability.
- `--stylize 0–1000` (default 100) — how hard Midjourney's aesthetic model pulls the image toward "pretty." Turn it down for documentary/technical subjects.
- Multi-prompts with relative weights: `photograph of a radio telescope::2 fog::1` — the `::N` weight biases the model toward the first term.
- **[established knowledge]** parameter ranges above are stable across MJ versions for years; live docs were 403-blocked this session, confirm exact current ranges at `docs.midjourney.com` before a big batch run.

**Gemini (conversational)** — there is no parameter syntax; the "parameters" are sentences inside the same chat turn, and refinement happens turn-by-turn:
```
Turn 1: "A photorealistic wide shot of a Yagi antenna array against a stormy dusk sky,
lit by a single warm sodium floodlight from below-left, shot on a 35mm lens,
palette restricted to deep navy #0C3350, warm amber #FFB238 and near-black,
compose with the right third of the frame empty sky for text overlay,
grainy, slightly underexposed, documentary mood. No text, no watermark. --ar 21:9"

Turn 2 (same thread): "Keep everything identical but make the sky darker and add
faint aurora-green streaks in the empty right third, low intensity, not overpowering the text zone."

Turn 3: "Now regenerate the same composition and lighting but replace the antenna
with a section of waveguide, still empty right third."
```
Turn 3 is the consistency trick: reusing the same thread carries style forward without needing a seed.

**Flux Kontext** — editing prompts describe the *change*, not the scene, because a reference image is already attached: `"Change the lighting to a cold blue rim light from the right, keep the subject and composition identical."`

**Ideogram** — put the literal text string in quotes inside the prompt, describe the typography style around it: `A risograph poster with the text "RADIO LAB" in bold grotesque sans, two-colour teal and orange misregistration, halftone dots`. Style reference is a separate image upload field, not a text parameter.

**Recraft** — colour is set via the UI hex picker *before* writing the text prompt; the text prompt then only needs to describe subject/composition, not colour, because the palette is already locked in the generation call.

### 2.3 Getting consistency across 3–5 images for one site

This is the single most valuable trick for making a generated set look "designed" instead of "rolled." Four techniques, in order of strength:

1. **A house-recipe paragraph, reused verbatim.** Write the technique + lighting + palette + mood + grain clauses *once* per project (see §8). For every image in the set, change only the subject and the empty-third placement; paste the rest unchanged. This alone gets you 80% of the way in Gemini, which has no seed/style-reference system.
2. **Chain reference images.** Generate image 1 first. Feed it back in as a style reference for images 2–5 — `--sref` in Midjourney, "style reference" upload in Ideogram/Recraft/Firefly, or literally "here is the first hero image [attach], generate a companion image in the exact same style for the following subject: …" in Gemini.
3. **Reuse seeds where exposed** (Midjourney, Flux, Ideogram). Same seed + same prompt skeleton + different subject noun often preserves lighting/colour grade almost exactly.
4. **Save a named Style once** (Recraft's Style objects, Firefly's Generative Match) instead of re-describing it — this is the most durable method for a project that will grow past 5 images, because the "recipe" lives as a reusable ID instead of prose that can drift between edits.

Across a whole site, also enforce consistency **outside** the generator: identical crop ratio per image slot, identical grain-overlay opacity, identical duotone filter values applied in post (§5). Post-processing consistency forgives a lot of generation-time drift.

## 3. Catalogue of unusual visual directions

55 named directions. Each has what it is, when it earns its place on a site, a radiophysics-faculty fit rating (★☆☆☆☆ weak → ★★★★★ ideal), and a complete copy-pasteable prompt template. Placeholders in `{BRACES}`. Swap `{HEX1/2/3}` for your site's actual palette.

#### A — Camera-less & alternative-process photography

##### 1. Photogram / camera-less photography (rayograph)
Objects laid directly on light-sensitive paper and exposed — pure silhouette and light, no lens ever involved. Suits a site that wants to say "we work with real physical signal, not stock imagery." **Radiophysics fit: ★★★☆☆**
```
Photogram / rayograph of {SUBJECT — a coil of enamelled copper wire and a handful of resistors}
arranged directly on light-sensitive paper, stark white silhouettes against deep {HEX1} background,
pure contact-print light and shadow with no lens distortion, soft halo where objects lifted off the paper,
fine paper-grain texture, Man Ray darkroom aesthetic, high contrast, single overhead exposure,
palette restricted to {HEX1} and {HEX2} only, leave the {LEFT/RIGHT} third pure unbroken {HEX1} for text,
no text, no letters, no watermark, no logo, --ar {16:9}
```

##### 2. Cyanotype
Prussian-blue monochrome contact print; UV-exposed, water-developed, a sharp silhouette from flat objects and a soft blur from anything three-dimensional. **Radiophysics fit: ★★★☆☆**
```
Cyanotype print of {SUBJECT — a schematic arrangement of vacuum tubes and wire},
deep Prussian blue #1B3A6B monochrome, objects pressed flat against the paper leaving sharp white
silhouettes, uneven hand-coated brush-stroke borders visible at the edges, subtle paper texture,
sun-bleached highlights, Anna Atkins botanical-print aesthetic, exposed under UV light,
leave the lower third a clean unbroken blue field for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {3:4}
```

##### 3. Platinum / palladium print
The most tonally delicate of the alt-processes — velvety matte blacks, no gloss, extraordinary midtone range. Suits an "archival, serious, institutional" register. **Radiophysics fit: ★★☆☆☆**
```
Platinum-palladium print of {SUBJECT — a large parabolic dish antenna at dawn},
extraordinarily long tonal range from velvet matte black to warm ivory white, completely matte
paper surface with no gloss, fine platinum grain visible under magnification, subtle sepia-warm
neutral tone, hand-coated edge irregularities, early-20th-century fine-art print aesthetic,
palette limited to warm greys and {HEX1}, empty sky in the upper third for text, no text, no watermark,
--ar {4:5}
```

##### 4. Gum bichromate print
Painterly, textured, layered pigment printing — visible brush texture, soft focus, colour laid in multiple passes. **Radiophysics fit: ★★☆☆☆**
```
Gum bichromate print of {SUBJECT}, layered pigment printing with visible brushstroke texture
at the edges, soft painterly focus, grainy watercolour-paper tooth showing through the image,
muted layered colour built from {HEX1} and {HEX2} passes with slight misregistration between
layers, early-1900s pictorialist photography aesthetic, no sharp detail, atmospheric and hand-made,
open unmarked paper margin on the {LEFT/RIGHT} for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {4:5}
```

##### 5. Wet plate collodion (tintype / ambrotype)
Shallow depth of field, syrupy tonality, characteristic edge vignetting and chemical streaks from hand-poured emulsion. **Radiophysics fit: ★★☆☆☆**
```
Wet plate collodion tintype of {SUBJECT}, narrow depth of field with dreamlike falloff to soft
blur, dark syrupy vignette at all four corners from hand-poured emulsion, faint comet-like
chemical streaks and swirl marks at the plate edges, metallic sheen in the shadows, 1860s
studio-portrait lighting, monochrome silver tones with a faint {HEX1} tint, dust and edge
imperfections, empty dark corner reserved for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {4:5}
```

##### 6. Anthotype
Made from crushed plant pigment, printed by sunlight alone over weeks — pastel, faded, organic, uneven. **Radiophysics fit: ★☆☆☆☆**
```
Anthotype print of {SUBJECT}, image formed from crushed plant-pigment emulsion bleached slowly
by sunlight, extremely soft pastel tonal range in muted {HEX1} and {HEX2}, uneven fading with
visible brush-coating edges, organic mottled texture, no hard blacks or whites anywhere in the
frame, botanical-print fragility, quiet and faded, wide low-contrast empty field for text,
no text, no watermark, --ar {1:1}
```

##### 7. Scanography (flatbed scanner photography)
Objects scanned directly — brutally flat lighting, pitch-black background falling off into nothing, extreme close focus. **Radiophysics fit: ★★★★☆**
```
Scanography of {SUBJECT — an open SDR dongle with visible PCB and shield can}, shot as if laid
directly on a flatbed scanner glass, harsh even frontal light with zero directional shadow,
background falling into pure unbroken {HEX1} black beyond the object's edge, extreme close
focus with a very shallow in-focus band, faint dust and fingerprint texture on the glass,
hyper-detailed material close-up, {HEX2} accent reflections on metal pins, wide black margin
on the {LEFT} for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {16:9}
```

#### B — Scientific & medical imaging

##### 8. X-ray imagery (radiograph)
Ghostly negative-density imagery revealing internal structure — dense material bright, void black. Reads instantly as "engineering, not decoration." **Radiophysics fit: ★★★★☆**
```
Radiographic X-ray image of {SUBJECT — a coaxial connector and a section of waveguide},
dense metal components glowing bright white, internal structure and threading visible through
the outer shell, pure black void background, soft grey gradient falloff at material edges,
clinical radiography contrast, monochrome with a faint {HEX1} tint on the brightest highlights,
wide black negative space in the {UPPER} third for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {21:9}
```

##### 9. CT imagery (volumetric scan)
Cross-sectional slices or a reconstructed volumetric render — layered, false-coloured, technical. Excellent for "we see inside things" messaging. **Radiophysics fit: ★★★★☆**
```
Volumetric CT-scan reconstruction of {SUBJECT — an antenna feed horn}, cross-sectional slices
stacked into a translucent 3D volume, false-colour density mapping from deep {HEX1} (low density)
through {HEX2} to bright {HEX3} (high density / metal), soft internal glow, medical-imaging
software aesthetic with a thin scan-line grid overlay, dark {HEX1} background, empty lower-left
quadrant for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {1:1}
```

##### 10. Electron micrograph (SEM false colour)
Native SEM images are greyscale with dramatic pseudo-3D shading from secondary-electron detection; false colour is a deliberate post-process convention, not a camera default — say so in the prompt. **Radiophysics fit: ★★★★☆**
```
Scanning electron micrograph of {SUBJECT — the surface of a silicon chip die / a ferrite
core's crystal structure}, extreme close-up with dramatic pseudo-3D topographic shading typical
of secondary-electron SEM imaging, native fine grain and shadow detail, then false-colour
post-processed in the SEM convention: {HEX1} for low areas, {HEX2} for mid elevations, {HEX3}
for peaks and edges, pure black background beyond the specimen, scientific-journal figure
aesthetic, empty flat region in the {CORNER} for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {1:1}
```

##### 11. Schlieren photography (airflow / heat)
Makes invisible density gradients visible — shimmering grey-scale (or rainbow-schlieren colour) plumes of heat or airflow around an object. Unusual, scientific, genuinely rare on websites. **Radiophysics fit: ★★★★★**
```
Schlieren photograph of heat rising off {SUBJECT — a power amplifier heatsink / a radio
transmitter chassis}, invisible thermal density gradients made visible as shimmering grey
plumes curling upward, dark grey-on-grey optical contrast typical of schlieren imaging
setups, knife-edge cutoff producing a subtle bright/dark split across the field, laboratory
black background, faint {HEX1} tint in the heat plume for rainbow-schlieren variant, clinical
and precise, wide still region at {BOTTOM} for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {21:9}
```

#### C — Energy & discharge phenomena

##### 12. Kirlian / corona discharge photography
Electric corona haloes frozen on film — glowing filament auras around leaves, coins, wire, connectors. Field-visualisation as literal subject. **Radiophysics fit: ★★★★★**
```
Kirlian corona-discharge photograph of {SUBJECT — a coiled length of copper wire / a brass
antenna connector}, blue-violet electrical corona haloing every edge, faint branching streamer
filaments fading into pure black, high-voltage discharge photography aesthetic shot on film
against a black backdrop, hyper-detailed glow structure, palette restricted to {HEX1} black,
{HEX2} violet-blue corona and a white-hot core, empty negative space in the {LEFT} third for
text, no text, no watermark, no logo, --ar {16:9}
```

##### 13. Plasma globe
Branching magenta-violet filaments reaching toward a touch point inside glass — instantly reads as "electricity, RF, energy." **Radiophysics fit: ★★★★☆**
```
Macro photograph of a plasma globe, branching magenta and violet filaments arcing from a
glowing core toward the glass surface, glass sphere reflections and fingerprints visible,
deep black surrounding darkness, long exposure capturing filament flicker as soft light
trails, palette of {HEX1} violet and {HEX2} magenta against black, empty dark quadrant at
{CORNER} for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {1:1}
```

##### 14. Smoke in a laser sheet
A thin plane of laser light slicing through smoke, revealing turbulent structure invisible in ambient light — flow visualisation as art. **Radiophysics fit: ★★★★☆**
```
Laser sheet illuminating drifting smoke in a dark laboratory, thin plane of {HEX1} laser
light revealing turbulent curling smoke structure suspended in black space, razor-sharp
light plane against pitch darkness elsewhere in frame, fine particulate detail, long exposure,
flow-visualisation aesthetic, palette restricted to {HEX1} laser green/red and void black,
wide black empty band along the {TOP} for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {21:9}
```

##### 15. Aurora / ionosphere imagery
Ionospheric plasma glow — directly on-theme for a radiophysics site studying propagation. **Radiophysics fit: ★★★★★**
```
Wide-angle night photograph of aurora borealis, curtains of {HEX1} green and {HEX2} violet
light rippling across a star-filled sky above a dark horizon line of {SUBJECT — a radio
telescope dish / an antenna field}, long exposure star trails just beginning, silhouetted
foreground equipment, crisp cold-air clarity, deep {HEX3} near-black sky at the top for
contrast, empty starfield region in the {UPPER} third for text, no text, no watermark,
--ar {21:9}
```

##### 16. UV-induced fluorescence photography
Object photographed under UV light so certain materials glow with colours invisible under normal light — eerie, scientific, unexpected. **Radiophysics fit: ★★☆☆☆**
```
UV-induced fluorescence photograph of {SUBJECT} under ultraviolet light in a dark room,
certain surfaces glowing vivid {HEX1} and {HEX2} against surroundings rendered near-black,
characteristic UV-photography colour shift, grainy high-ISO texture, forensic/mineralogy
photography aesthetic, glowing highlight detail with zero ambient fill light, dark unlit
region in the {LOWER} third for text, no text, no watermark, --ar {4:5}
```

#### D — Time & motion

##### 17. Long-exposure light painting
Hand-drawn trails of light traced through darkness during a long shutter exposure. Great for "signal path" and "waveform" metaphors. **Radiophysics fit: ★★★★☆**
```
Long-exposure light-painting photograph in a dark studio, continuous glowing trail of
{HEX1} light tracing the outline of {SUBJECT — a sine wave / an antenna radiation pattern}
against pitch-black background, sharp light-source core with soft bloom falloff, faint
secondary {HEX2} trail crossing behind it, tripod-still background with zero camera shake,
long-exposure night-photography grain, empty black field on the {RIGHT} for text, no text,
no watermark, --ar {16:9}
```

##### 18. Chronophotography (Marey / Muybridge)
Multiple sequential exposures of motion overlaid on one frame or laid out in a grid — the original data-visualisation photography. **Radiophysics fit: ★★★☆☆**
```
Chronophotographic sequence in the style of Étienne-Jules Marey, {SUBJECT — a rotating
antenna / a mechanical relay arm} captured as overlapping sequential exposures on a single
frame, semi-transparent ghost repetitions showing motion path, monochrome sepia-grey tones
```

## 4. Backgrounds that text can live on

Four reusable clauses. Append any one of them, verbatim, to the end of any prompt in §3.

**Empty-third / empty-quadrant clause:**
```
Compose with the {LEFT/RIGHT/UPPER/LOWER} third of the frame left deliberately empty and
low-detail — flat shadow, out-of-focus falloff, plain sky, or unbroken backdrop — dark
enough (below roughly 20% luminance) for white text to sit on top with no additional
overlay needed; keep the subject and all fine detail confined to the opposite two-thirds;
avoid any small pattern, bright highlight, or texture in that zone that would fight with
overlaid type.
```

**Controlled-contrast / "plate" clause** (for a dark hero plate):
```
Keep overall contrast low to moderate and avoid pure white highlights or pure black
crushed shadows anywhere in frame; light the scene so the darkest 40% of the image sits
in a narrow tonal band around {HEX_DARK}, giving a "plate" for text and UI elements to
sit on without additional darkening in post.
```
For a light plate, invert: hold highlights in a narrow band around a near-white `{HEX_LIGHT}` and avoid deep shadow.

**Vignette clause:**
```
Add a soft natural vignette darkening toward all four edges of the frame, heaviest in
the {CORNER/EDGE} that will carry text, light enough elsewhere that it reads as optical
falloff rather than a heavy-handed filter.
```

**Seamless / tileable texture clause** (for background-image patterns, not hero photography):
```
Seamless tileable texture, edge-to-edge repeating pattern with no visible seam at any
border, flat even lighting with no directional shadow, gradient, or vignette that would
reveal the tile boundary when repeated; design the repeat unit so it tiles cleanly at
{512×512 / 1024×1024}.
```
Generators do not guarantee true seamlessness even with this wording — always test-tile the result (duplicate it in a 2×2 grid in code) before shipping; treat the prompt as reducing edit work, not eliminating it.

**"Survives a colour overlay" clause** — the most important one for a site that will apply a duotone or brand-colour wash in CSS afterward:
```
Shoot with flat, even, documentary lighting and avoid a heavy colour grade baked into
the image — no strong colour cast, no crushed blacks, no blown highlights; keep the
tonal range roughly within 10–90% so a duotone colour overlay can be applied afterward
without losing shadow or highlight detail; render primarily in luminance/contrast rather
than saturated colour.
```
This works because `mix-blend-mode: color` / `luminosity` and the `feColorMatrix` duotone recipe in §5 both **read the image as a greyscale luminance map** and repaint it — an image that is already saturated and colour-graded fights the overlay instead of cooperating with it. Ask the generator for something closer to a black-and-white photograph with correct tonal placement, and let CSS/SVG do the colour.

---

## 5. Post-processing after generation

### 5.1 Crop the generator's inset frame
Gemini, Midjourney and Ideogram all occasionally leave a soft vignette, a faint border, or slightly inconsistent edge framing baked into the output (an artefact of how the model was trained on framed photographs). Crop **2–4% off every edge** before using an image full-bleed — treat this as a mandatory step in the pipeline, not a fix for occasional bad luck.

### 5.2 Colour-grade to the site palette

**CSS duotone via `mix-blend-mode`** (fast, good enough for most cases):
```css
.hero { position: relative; overflow: hidden; }
.hero img { display: block; width: 100%; filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05); }
.hero::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute; inset: 0;
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #0C3350, #4DFFB4);
  mix-blend-mode: color;      /* try luminosity, multiply, screen too */
  opacity: .85;
}
```
`color` and `luminosity` are the two modes that actually behave like a photographic duotone (they read the base image's own luminance and repaint hue/saturation); `multiply`/`screen` behave more like a tint and are better for a subtle wash than a full recolour. Source: [MDN — mix-blend-mode](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/mix-blend-mode).

**Precise SVG duotone via `feColorMatrix` + `feComponentTransfer`** (the "correct" recipe — desaturate, then remap black→shadow-hex and white→highlight-hex):
```html
<svg width="0" height="0" aria-hidden="true">
  <filter id="duotone">
    <feColorMatrix type="matrix" values="
      0.33 0.33 0.33 0 0
      0.33 0.33 0.33 0 0
      0.33 0.33 0.33 0 0
      0    0    0    1 0" result="gray"/>
    <feComponentTransfer color-interpolation-filters="sRGB">
      <!-- shadow hex #0A0E12 -> highlight hex #4DFFB4, per channel -->
      <feFuncR type="table" tableValues="0.039 0.302"/>
      <feFuncG type="table" tableValues="0.055 1.000"/>
      <feFuncB type="table" tableValues="0.071 0.706"/>
    </feComponentTransfer>
  </filter>
</svg>
<img src="hero.avif" style="filter:url(#duotone)" alt="…">
```
Convert each hex channel to 0–1 (`#4DFFB4` → R 0.302, G 1.000, B 0.706) and drop those two numbers straight into the matching `tableValues`. This is deterministic, GPU-cheap, and — unlike the CSS overlay trick — works identically as a native `<img>` filter with no extra DOM layer.

### 5.3 Grain overlay
```css
.grain::before {
  content: "";
  position: absolute; inset: -10%;
  background-image: url("data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><filter id='n'><feTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.9' numOctaves='2' stitchTiles='stitch'/></filter><rect width='100%25' height='100%25' filter='url(%23n)'/></svg>");
  opacity: .05; mix-blend-mode: overlay; pointer-events: none;
}
```
Keep opacity between 3–7%; this is what unifies a set of images shot/generated at different times into "one material" — apply the *same* grain layer, same opacity, across every image on the site, not a re-generated one per image.

### 5.4 AVIF / WebP with real quality targets
- **AVIF** first: ~30–50% smaller than an equivalent-quality WebP, ~50%+ smaller than JPEG. For a full-bleed hero (1920–2560px wide), target a **file size band (150–400KB)** rather than a fixed quality number — encoders' quality scales aren't comparable 1:1; use `sharp`/`squoosh`/`avifenc` and eyeball at 100%/200% zoom until banding appears in the empty-third gradient (the gradient is always the first thing to band).
- **WebP** as the fallback layer, quality ≈ 75–82.
- **JPEG** progressive, quality ≈ 80, only as the final `<img>` fallback for old crawlers/share-preview bots.
```html
<picture>
  <source type="image/avif" srcset="hero-640.avif 640w, hero-1280.avif 1280w, hero-1920.avif 1920w, hero-2560.avif 2560w, hero-3840.avif 3840w" sizes="100vw">
  <source type="image/webp" srcset="hero-640.webp 640w, hero-1280.webp 1280w, hero-1920.webp 1920w, hero-2560.webp 2560w">
  <img src="hero-1920.jpg" srcset="hero-640.jpg 640w, hero-1280.jpg 1280w, hero-1920.jpg 1920w" sizes="100vw" alt="…" loading="eager" fetchpriority="high">
</picture>
```
Source: [MDN mix-blend-mode](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/mix-blend-mode) confirms browser support baseline; AVIF/WebP quality guidance above is standard web-performance practice, not a single-source claim.

### 5.5 LQIP / blur-up
Cheapest good option: generate a ~20px-wide version, base64-inline it as the `background-image` of the container, blur it with CSS, and cross-fade to the real image on load:
```css
.hero { background-size: cover; background-image: var(--lqip); }
.hero img { opacity: 0; transition: opacity .4s ease; }
.hero img.loaded { opacity: 1; }
```
For even smaller payloads, trace the 20px LQIP as an SVG (the "SQIP" technique) instead of embedding a blurred raster — a few hundred bytes instead of a few kilobytes.

### 5.6 Making it look like part of the design system, not a stock photo
- **One post-processing pipeline, run over every image** — same crop percentage, same grain layer, same duotone matrix, same corner radius (usually *none*, full-bleed). Consistency of *treatment* matters more than consistency of *subject*.
- **No drop-shadow card treatment.** Stock-photo sites float images in rounded cards with soft shadows; an art-directed site runs them full-bleed behind type, edge-to-edge, with the empty-third doing the compositional work instead of a card boundary.
- **Typography sits on the image, not beside it.** If the empty-third clause (§4) worked, the headline literally overlaps the photograph — that overlap is what reads as "designed," not "illustrated."
- **Keep the grain/duotone identical across photo *and* any procedural/SVG elements on the same page** (§7.2) — that's what makes a hand-generated hero and a hand-coded diagram look like they came from the same studio.

## 6. Legal / ethical

| Tool | Commercial-use terms, 2026 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Google Gemini / Imagen** | Generated content usable commercially under Google's Generative AI terms; **every image carries an invisible SynthID watermark** that survives cropping, filtering, and lossy compression | [Verified](https://deepmind.google/technologies/synthid/): watermark doesn't affect visual quality but is detectable by Google's own tools — relevant if a competitor or press outlet runs your hero image through a SynthID checker |
| **Midjourney** | Paid subscription required for **any** usage rights (no free tier since 2023); Standard/Pro/Mega General Commercial Terms apply automatically once subscribed; orgs with **>$1M prior-year gross revenue** need Pro or Mega, not Standard | Images are **public by default** (visible in the community feed) unless on a Pro/Mega plan with Stealth Mode enabled — relevant before a brand reveal |
| **Flux (BFL)** | Licence depends on the exact variant: `schnell`/`klein` = **Apache-2.0** (full commercial + redistribution); `dev`/`Kontext-dev` = **non-commercial research licence**; `pro`/`flex`/`ultra` = commercial via BFL's API or partner hosts (Replicate, Krea, Adobe) under normal paid-API terms | [Verified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Forest_Labs) — check the specific variant before self-hosting; `dev` weights are *not* cleared for a commercial site even though they're downloadable |
| **Ideogram** | Freemium; historically grants commercial rights on both free and paid tiers (unlike Midjourney) — **[established knowledge, verify current wording at ideogram.ai/terms before client work]**; 4.0 weights are Apache-2.0 for self-hosting | Best text-rendering tool, so also the one most likely to accidentally reproduce a trademarked logotype if asked for one — don't ask |
| **Recraft** | Paid-plan commercial rights; free-tier limits apply | Output is often further hand-edited as SVG, which in practice makes the IP position cleaner — the shipped asset is a derivative you modified, not a raw model output |
| **Freepik / Magnific** | Freepik Premium licence needed for full commercial rights on Freepik-*sourced* assets; a Magnific upscale of **your own** already-commercial image inherits your existing rights over that base image | |
| **Krea** | Commercial rights generally follow the underlying model's licence per-generation (check which model served the request) | Aggregator — the licence is not uniform across everything Krea can produce |
| **Luma / Runway** | Paid-plan commercial rights; free/watermarked tiers are evaluation-only | |
| **Adobe Firefly** | Adobe offers **IP-indemnification ("commercially safe") for Enterprise customers** using Firefly-generated content; training data is billed as Adobe Stock + licensed + public domain | [Verified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe_Firefly) — this claim has been **publicly contested** (reporting that some training incorporated competitor-model output); treat "commercially safe" as Adobe's marketing position, not an uncontested legal fact, when the stakes are high |

**The rule that overrides every tool's ToS: do not generate real, identifiable people, and do not generate existing logos/crests/trademarks.**
- Every major generator's usage policy already prohibits generating real public figures in deceptive or commercial-endorsement contexts, and prohibits reproducing protected trademarks — but the deeper reason to avoid it is that **right-of-publicity and trademark law apply regardless of what a vendor's terms of service permit.** A tool allowing you to generate a likeness does not make using it legal in your jurisdiction.
- For a **university faculty site** specifically: never prompt "a photo of professor {real name}" — commission real photography or use a photo the person consented to. Never generate a fake university crest/logo — vectorise or request the real one from the institution's brand office. Never generate an image that could pass as a real named facility's (e.g. a specific radio telescope's) proprietary control-room photo in a way that implies a false affiliation or partnership.
- Generated **people in general** (unnamed, generic) are fine for atmosphere shots, but faces are the least reliable output of every tool on this list (uncanny valley, wrong hand/ear counts) — this is a craft reason, on top of the legal one, to lean on the object/phenomenon-focused catalogue in §3 instead of generating students/staff.

## 7. Alternatives when generation is wrong

### 7.1 Public-domain and CC0 archives

| Archive | Licence status | Why it's useful for a radiophysics/science site |
|---|---|---|
| **NASA** (images.nasa.gov, science.nasa.gov) | Public domain (US government work); **exceptions**: some contractor-supplied images are separately copyrighted and marked as such; can't imply NASA endorsement; can't use current employee likenesses commercially | [Verified](https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/) — huge trove of radio-astronomy, satellite, deep-space-network antenna imagery, directly on-topic |
| **ESA** | CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO for most imagery (attribution + share-alike required, **not** CC0) **[established knowledge — esa.int copyright page blocked automated fetch]** | European radio-astronomy and satellite-comms imagery |
| **CERN** | CC-BY-4.0 for most media **[established knowledge — home.cern copyright page returned 404 on this pass]** | Particle-physics instrumentation photography has a strong aesthetic overlap with RF/antenna hardware macro shots |
| **Wellcome Collection** | Hundreds of thousands of images tagged public domain/CC0, especially historical scientific and medical illustration | Excellent source for alt-process (§3A) *reference material*, and for genuinely antique technical illustration |
| **Smithsonian Open Access** | **4.9M+ CC0** images since Feb 2020, including National Air and Space Museum holdings (antennas, satellites, early radio) | |
| **Library of Congress** ("Free to Use and Reuse" sets) | No known copyright restrictions on curated sets | Deep historic photo and technical-drawing archive |
| **Internet Archive** | Mixed — **licence varies per item**, always check the individual item's rights field | Huge trove of scanned technical manuals and radio/electronics ephemera — a real source for the microfiche/blueprint aesthetic rather than a simulated one |
| **Europeana** | Aggregator of European museums/libraries; filter by rights statement (CC0 / Public Domain Mark / CC BY) | |
| **Rijksmuseum (Rijksstudio)** | Public-domain works downloadable in ultra-high resolution for free, explicit open policy | |
| **Met Museum Open Access** | **492,000+ CC0** images via API since 2017 | |
| **Public Domain Review** | Curated essays with high-res scans of unusual/obscure public-domain material | [Verified](https://publicdomainreview.org/about/) — a genuinely good source for finding real Chladni-figure plates, real cyanotypes, real chronophotography instead of simulating them |
| **USGS** | Public domain (US government work), same endorsement caveat as NASA | Satellite, topographic, geological, ionospheric imagery |
| **NOAA** | Public domain (US government work) | Aurora, ionosphere, atmospheric imagery — directly relevant to propagation/radiophysics themes |
| **Unsplash** | Commercial and non-commercial use permitted, **no attribution required**; can't resell unmodified, can't build a competing stock service | [Verified](https://unsplash.com/license) — the catch for an *award-winning* site is that everyone else can grab the same photo; treat as a fallback, not a hero source |
| **Pexels** | Same profile as Unsplash: commercial free, no attribution required, can't resell unmodified or use as a trademark | [Verified](https://www.pexels.com/license/) |

### 7.2 Procedural / generated-in-code alternatives

For a radiophysics site in particular, several of the "unusual directions" in §3 describe **real, measurable data** — and drawing the real thing in SVG/canvas/WebGL is often both cheaper and more credible to the target audience than asking a model to imagine one:

- **SVG** — generative line-field patterns, antenna radiation-pattern diagrams, radar-sweep radial gradients, isometric technical diagrams. Infinitely scalable, tiny file size, trivially recolourable via CSS custom properties, zero uncanny-valley risk.
- **Canvas / WebGL shaders** — an *actually computed* oscilloscope/Lissajous curve (`x = sin(a·t + δ)`, `y = sin(b·t)`) is more accurate than a photo of one and costs nothing to re-skin in the house palette; a real FFT run on a real (or synthetic) audio/RF signal produces a real spectrogram/waterfall plot (§3.25) instead of an imitation; Perlin/simplex flow-field shaders approximate schlieren-like or smoke-like motion live and respond to scroll/mouse; shader-based glass caustics or chrome (Three.js / react-three-fiber) render in real time and can rotate with the viewport.
- **When procedural beats generated, specifically:** when the subject *is* data (spectrogram, Lissajous, antenna pattern, Smith chart) — draw the real thing, it is more credible to a physics-literate visitor than a plausible fake; when guaranteed seamless tiling or exact brand hex with zero colour drift matters more than photographic richness; when page-weight/performance budgets are tight (a shader background can beat a 300KB AVIF hero); when the site's entire pitch is "we do real engineering" — a genuine plotted dataset outperforms a beautiful imitation of one every time a technical visitor looks closely.

## 8. House recipe

### 8.1 Reusable skeleton

```
[SHOT TYPE] of [SUBJECT — 2-3 recognisable specific details],
[TECHNIQUE / PROCESS clause — pick one from §3],
lit by [LIGHT SOURCE, direction, quality, colour temperature],
captured as if [CAMERA / FILM / LENS, or render engine],
palette strictly [HEX1 role, HEX2 role, HEX3 role] — no colours outside this set,
composed with [SUBJECT placement] and the [THIRD/QUADRANT] left empty, low-detail
and [dark/light] for overlaid text,
mood: [3 adjectives],
[GRAIN / TEXTURE clause],
no text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, no logo, no frame or border,
--ar [RATIO] [tool-specific params]
```

Fill the technique, lighting, palette, mood and grain slots **once** for a project, then reuse that filled-in paragraph unchanged across every image in the set — only the subject and the empty-zone placement should change. This is the "house recipe" referenced in §2.3, applied.

### 8.2 The faculty's house palette

Fixed across all six examples below, so the set reads as one design system:

| Role | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Void ink | `#0A0E12` | deep background / shadow |
| Radar blue | `#0C3350` | primary dark field |
| Phosphor green | `#4DFFB4` | signal / accent glow |
| Telemetry amber | `#FFB238` | secondary accent, warm counterpoint |
| Waveguide silver | `#B8C2CC` | metal / neutral highlight |
| Copper / ferrite | `#B5732E` | hardware warmth |

### 8.3 Six fully-written prompts for the radiophysics faculty site

**1 — Homepage hero (Kirlian corona discharge, §3.12):**
```
Extreme close-up Kirlian corona-discharge photograph of a brass coaxial connector and
a short length of stripped copper wire, blue-violet electrical corona haloing every
edge, faint branching streamer filaments fading into pure black, high-voltage discharge
photography aesthetic shot on film against a black backdrop, hyper-detailed filament
glow with fine grain, palette strictly void black #0A0E12, phosphor-green #4DFFB4 corona
and a white-hot core — no colours outside this set, composed with the connector filling
the lower two-thirds and the upper third left empty, low-detail, near-black for overlaid
headline text, mood: precise, nocturnal, electric, fine 35mm-equivalent film grain with
slight halation on the brightest filaments, no text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark,
no logo, no frame or border, --ar 21:9 --style raw
```

**2 — "Research" section (radio-telescope false-colour map, §3.26):**
```
Wide false-colour radio-astronomy emission map in the style of a VLA observation,
looping filamentary structure rendered smoothly from deep radar-blue #0C3350 through
mid-tone teal to bright phosphor-green #4DFFB4 at peak flux, star-black #0A0E12
background, scientific-publication figure clarity with a subtle beam-size ellipse
implied in the lower-right corner but no legible labels, composed with the emission
structure concentrated in the right two-thirds and the left third left genuinely
empty, low-detail, near-black for body text, mood: vast, precise, luminous, faint
sensor-noise grain across the dark field, no text, no numbers, no watermark, no logo,
no frame or border, --ar 16:9
```

**3 — "Signals & DSP" section (oscilloscope Lissajous, §3.19):**
```
Macro photograph of a CRT oscilloscope screen displaying a glowing phosphor-green
#4DFFB4 Lissajous curve against void-black #0A0E12, soft bloom and slight screen
curvature visible, faint horizontal scan-line texture and phosphor grain, dark bezel
framing all four edges of frame, subtle warm amber #FFB238 reflection of a lab light
in the glass corner, deep black surrounding the glow with a long persistence trail
on the curve, composed with the curve centred and the entire dark bezel border left
empty and low-detail for a caption to sit on, mood: hypnotic, exact, luminous, fine
video-grain texture, no text, no letters, no watermark, no logo, no frame or border,
--ar 1:1
```

**4 — "Hardware labs" section (ferrite/copper coil macro, §3.53):**
```
Macro photograph of hand-wound copper coils on ferrite toroid cores, warm copper
#B5732E wire catching a single raking highlight against matte dark radar-blue #0C3350
ferrite, precise regular winding pattern, shallow depth of field with the nearest
winding sharp and the rest falling into soft blur, fine dust and light tarnish
texture on the copper, macro product-photography clarity, palette strictly copper
#B5732E, radar-blue #0C3350 and waveguide-silver #B8C2CC highlights, composed with
the sharp coil in the left two-thirds and the blurred right third left low-detail
and dark for text, mood: tactile, warm, precise, fine macro-lens grain, no text, no
letters, no watermark, no logo, no frame or border, --ar 4:5
```

**5 — "Programmes / admissions" section (blueprint technical drawing, §3.29):**
```
Technical blueprint drawing of a log-periodic antenna array, crisp waveguide-silver
#B8C2CC linework on a solid radar-blue #0C3350 ground, precise orthographic projection
with dimension lines and cross-hatch shading on curved surfaces, faint paper fold
-crease texture, engineering-drafting aesthetic, phosphor-green #4DFFB4 accent linework
on two callout details with no legible numbers, composed with the drawing occupying
the lower two-thirds and the upper third left as unbroken blueprint-blue field for a
headline, mood: precise, institutional, calm, subtle paper-grain texture throughout,
no text, no numbers, no watermark, no logo, no frame or border, --ar 16:9
```

**6 — "Propagation / RF power" section (schlieren heat, §3.11):**
```
Schlieren photograph of heat rising off a power-amplifier heatsink, invisible thermal
density gradients made visible as shimmering plumes in tones between radar-blue
#0C3350 and phosphor-green #4DFFB4, dark grey-on-near-black optical contrast typical
of schlieren imaging setups, knife-edge cutoff producing a subtle bright/dark split
across the field, laboratory void-black #0A0E12 background, clinical and precise,
composed with the heatsink and rising plume in the lower two-thirds and the upper
third left as calm, low-detail dark field for text, mood: precise, invisible-made-
visible, quietly dramatic, fine grain, no text, no letters, no watermark, no logo,
no frame or border, --ar 21:9
```

Generate all six in the same Gemini chat thread where possible, in this order — hero first, then feed it back in each subsequent turn as "match the lighting and grain of the previous image" — to squeeze extra consistency out of a tool with no seed system.
